title: Verify code-search shard provenance before merge
description:
Problem: shard merge validates the database container but trusts imported document paths, snippets, line ranges, hashes, search text, embeddings, and timestamps. A stale or mismatched shard can pollute the primary index with false source evidence.

Desired outcome: shard rows are treated as untrusted acceleration data and become searchable only after local provenance checks succeed.

Scope:
- Require imported document paths to resolve under an allowed repository root.
- Verify local file existence and compare current content hashes with shard claims.
- Recompute snippets and line ranges from local content instead of trusting shard payloads.
- Record shard digest, merge time, actor, and source revision when available.
- Keep unverified rows staged or rejected with a visible reason.
- Out of scope: changing general code-search ranking.

Acceptance criteria:
- A shard built from a different or changed checkout cannot silently become authoritative.
- Imported rows with missing files, path escapes, hash mismatches, or invalid ranges are rejected or staged.
- Accepted snippets and line ranges are derived from the current local source.
- Provenance is queryable without exposing sensitive source content.
- Tests cover valid, stale, tampered, and path-escaping shard rows.

Validation:
- Run focused shard-merge and code-search integrity tests.
- Run the code-search benchmark smoke validation.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
